questions.title: Which television series will win Outstanding Comedy Series at the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Television Academy's official winner announcement for Outstanding Comedy Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards in 2026. questions.current_reasoning: Upgrading Widow's Bay (0.72 -> 0.79) and trimming Hacks (0.255 -> 0.19) four days before the Sept 14 ceremony based on decisive Sept 8-10 post-Creative Arts market and expert consolidation. Covers.com's live Sept 10 (12:53 PM ET) Kalshi real-money market now prices Widow's Bay at 81%, Hacks at 18%, and Shrinking at 1%, while Gold Derby (Sept 8) reported double-digit gains for Widow's Bay in Comedy Series, Supporting Actress, and Directing following its 8 Creative Arts wins (including Casting and Guest Actress over five Hacks nominees). We apply modest 2-point shrinkage from Kalshi (0.79 vs 0.81) given Hacks's history of winning Series after weak Creative Arts nights and its finale Single-Cam Editing win; Shrinking enters #3 (0.007) alongside Margo's Got Money Troubles (0.006) and Abbott Elementary (0.005; sum 0.998).

questions.title: Which stadium will UEFA select to host the 2029 men's Champions League final?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UEFA's official announcement awarding hosting rights for the 2029 men's Champions League final, or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution Date : Resolve when UEFA publicly announces its venue selection. Subsequent venue changes will not alter the answer. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the selected stadium.
questions.current_reasoning: Modestly upgrading Camp Nou (0.65 -> 0.70) over Wembley Stadium (0.35 -> 0.30) in this confirmed two-stadium race ahead of the UEFA Executive Committee decision in Thessaloniki on September 15. A fresh Sept 9 EFE/Infobae pre-vote report explicitly identifies Camp Nou as the favorite over Wembley, highlighting that the renovated Barcelona venue will be Europe's largest stadium (104,600 capacity, first UCL final since 1999) whereas Wembley is already locked in to host both semifinals and the final of Euro 2028 less than a year earlier (after also hosting the 2024 UCL final). Combined with Barcelona already playing La Liga matches back at Camp Nou and improved Laporta-Ceferin relations, Camp Nou warrants ~70% while keeping 30% on Wembley given Madrid's 2027 Metropolitano final and secret ExCo ballot risk.

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-06 check (Exa + Sept 2 Reuters/Straits Times investigation 'US, China arm for space warfare: hunter satellites and orbital weapons'): No country has yet publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons. Crucially, the Sept 2 Reuters report sharpens the asymmetry in public-acknowledgment propensity: China's Foreign Ministry reiterated on the record that Beijing opposes space weaponization and insists its spaceplane/Shiyan missions are peaceful/experimental, and Moscow continues denying its nuclear ASAT program. By contrast, US SPACECOM head Gen. Stephen Whiting is openly arguing for an active warfighting posture and orbital interceptors, incoming Space Force CSO Lt. Gen. Douglas Schiess led the newly disclosed US-UK orbital proximity operation, and the Space Force already broke silence in June with a rare disclosure of an earthbound L3Harris ASAT jammer—building toward potential deterrence disclosures at the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference. Lifting United States (0.49 -> 0.53) while trimming Russia (0.25 -> 0.23) and China (0.12 -> 0.10), with France (0.08, Yoda) and India (0.03) steady (sum = 0.97).

questions.title: Which city will be awarded hosting rights for the 2029 World Athletics Championships?
questions.background: World Athletics selects the host cities for its biennial outdoor track-and-field world championships.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : World Athletics' official announcement awarding hosting rights for the 2029 World Athletics Championships. Resolution : Resolve when World Athletics first publicly announces the successful host city. The initial award determines the answer, regardless of any subsequent changes. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the name of the selected city, not the country or stadium.
questions.current_reasoning: Key August 10-14 bidding confirmations (BBC Sport, Reuters/Straits Times, KBC, Citizen Digital): The formal bid deadline passed on Aug 5 and virtual presentations to Sebastian Coe and the World Athletics Council took place on Aug 13, confirming ONLY four cities are officially bidding for the 2029 and 2031 World Athletics Championships: London, Nairobi, Rome, and Munich. New Delhi did not submit a bid and is removed (0.04 -> 0.00). Coe confirmed both 2029 and 2031 hosts will be announced simultaneously on Sept 15 after the Budapest Ultimate Championships. Reallocating the eliminated 0.04 and prior residual across the four confirmed bidders: London rises 0.52 -> 0.56 as the clearest 2029 fit (resolved West Ham/London Stadium deal specifically for Sept 2029, full UK Govt/Mayor backing, European rotation after Tokyo 2025 & Beijing 2027, and a natural London 2029 / Nairobi 2031 pairing); Nairobi rises 0.20 -> 0.22 after formally submitting and delivering President Ruto's ironclad state guarantee on Aug 13 for Africa's first hosting; proven European hosts Rome (0.11 -> 0.12) and Munich (0.10) remain live Council alternatives (sum = 1.00 across the complete four-city field).

questions.title: Which club will win the 2026 Campeones Cup?
questions.background: The Campeones Cup is an annual match between the previous season’s MLS Cup champion and the winner of Mexico’s Campeón de Campeones.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official competition result published by Major League Soccer, supported by reliable match reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the club officially declared the winner of the 2026 Campeones Cup once the match has concluded, including extra time or a penalty shootout if required. Accepted Answer Format : The winning club’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Modestly trimming Inter Miami CF (-0.03 to 0.55) and lifting Cruz Azul (+0.03 to 0.45) ahead of the Sept 16 single-leg Campeones Cup final at Nu Stadium following Miami's Sept 5/6 MLS result and a full September schedule comparison. Although Lionel Messi stayed sharp in his first match since retiring from Argentina (2 assists, crossbar free kick) and Casemiro plus Luis Suarez scored, Miami were held 2-2 at home by lowly Atlanta United (6-13-3, 21 pts)—conceding two goals and two penalties (one saved by Dayne St. Clair, one scored by Breel Embolo in the 87') with Casemiro deployed at center-back, leaving Miami with just one win in their last seven MLS matches. Moreover, verified September calendars show Inter Miami face heavier pre-final congestion (4 matches in 11 days: Sept 5 Atlanta after a 90-min lightning delay, Sept 9 away at playoff-contending Chicago Fire, Sept 12 vs Eastern Conference-leading Nashville SC [16-2-4], then Sept 16 Cruz Azul), whereas 10th-placed Cruz Azul (3W-3L, playing winless Santos Laguna tonight Sept 6) have no midweek game before their Sept 12 Clasico Joven vs Liga MX leaders Club America. Miami remain deserved ~55% favorites on home soil with a non-traveling Messi and Cruz Azul's America/travel/Monterrey (Sept 19) rotation dilemma reported by AS Mexico, but 0.55/0.45 better prices Miami's defensive fragility and veteran fatigue.

questions.current_reasoning: Modestly concentrating probability onto top two crises Sudan (0.44 -> 0.47) and Yemen (0.28 -> 0.30) based on Sept 10 Al Jazeera and Arab News reporting during UNGA opening week. Trimming quieter crises Myanmar (0.065 -> 0.05), South Sudan (0.055 -> 0.045), and Democratic Republic of the Congo (0.045 -> 0.035; sum 0.900, residual 0.100).
